shared_elements: animal head in profile with prominent beak/snout
quadruped or crouching animal with visible limbs
anthropomorphic figure with arms bent toward the body
schematic incised linear detail (rows of short strokes)
justification: Both are tall pale stone blocks organised as a vertical stack of creature-forms, and both include a beaked/snouted animal head above a crouching figure whose splayed fingers are cut as parallel grooves, which is a fairly specific correspondence. The decisive difference is technique and format: A is flat, shallow relief and incision confined to the faces of an architectural slab, while B is a fully three-dimensional carving in which the figures project into the round and dominate the mass of the stone.
